ports.name: keys
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys to watch. Leave blank to react to every change in the store.

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.tooltip: Reason reported on Error when this update is rolled back. Wire the server error here.

ports.name: transactionId
ports.tooltip: Leave blank to let the node generate one. Set it to commit or roll back a specific update when several are in flight.

ports.name: timeout
ports.tooltip: Roll back automatically after this long with no answer. Zero disables the deadline.

ports.name: onDispose
ports.tooltip: What happens to updates still in flight when this node is removed. Rolling back keeps the store honest; keeping the value suits fire-and-forget actions the user navigates away from.

ports.name: trackKeys
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys to record. Blank records the whole store. Undo then writes only these keys and leaves the rest alone. Changing this clears the history.

ports.name: maxHistory
ports.tooltip: How many entries to keep. The oldest are dropped first. An unbounded history is a memory leak.

ports.name: coalesceMs
ports.tooltip: Fold successive changes to the same keys within this many milliseconds into one undo step, so typing is one undo rather than one per keystroke. 0 records every change separately.

ports.name: enabled
ports.tooltip: Turning this off pauses recording. The history already collected is kept.

ports.name: snapshotData
ports.tooltip: Snapshot to restore instead of the named one — a previously exported "Snapshot" output. Leave blank to restore by name.

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.tooltip: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal.

ports.name: protocols
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake.

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.tooltip: First backoff delay. Each further attempt doubles it, up to Max Reconnect Delay.

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.tooltip: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage. 0 disables retrying; a negative value means unlimited.

ports.name: jitter
ports.tooltip: Spread reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window.

ports.name: heartbeatInterval
ports.tooltip: Send Heartbeat Message this often while open. 0 disables it. Only enable this if your server expects the message — it is application data, not a protocol ping frame.

ports.name: heartbeatReply
ports.tooltip: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with. It is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and — if it stops arriving — treated as a dead connection. Leave empty to only send heartbeats.

ports.name: message
ports.tooltip: Value to send. Objects are JSON-serialized; ArrayBuffers and typed arrays are sent as binary frames.

ports.name: messageType
ports.tooltip: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text. Binary forces text and objects to be UTF-8 encoded first.

ports.name: whenDisconnected
ports.tooltip: What a Send does while the connection is not open. Queue holds it (in order) until the socket reopens; Drop discards it and counts it; Report Error also sets Last Error and fires On Error.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.tooltip: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted in Dropped. 0 or less means unlimited, which can grow without bound during a long outage.

ports.name: eventTypes
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to. Only needed for the EventSource transport, which delivers a named event only to a listener registered in advance; the Fetch transport delivers every event type.

ports.name: textPath
ports.tooltip: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path — for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, choices.0.delta.content. Leave blank for a stream that sends bare text. Whatever it names ends up on the Text output, which is always a string.

ports.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd
ports.tooltip: Reconnect when the server closes the stream cleanly. Off by default: an agent response stream is finite, and reconnecting would re-issue the request and start the response again.

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.tooltip: First retry delay. Doubles per consecutive failure, up to the maximum.

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.tooltip: 0 means keep retrying. Otherwise the connection reports an error after this many consecutive failures.

ports.name: dedupeById
ports.tooltip: Drop events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes from the last event id cannot re-deliver messages. Turn off if your server reuses ids for distinct events.

ports.name: delimiter
ports.tooltip: Message boundary. Leave empty to accumulate everything without splitting — the mode a token stream wants.

ports.name: maxLength
ports.tooltip: Cap on the pending buffer. Overflow drops the oldest characters and is reported on Dropped Characters.

ports.name: maxMessages
ports.tooltip: Cap on retained complete messages; the oldest are dropped first. 0 keeps them all, which grows forever.

ports.name: maxLength
ports.tooltip: Cap on unparsed text held while waiting for a value to complete. Exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error, rather than growing without limit on a malformed stream.

ports.name: pattern
ports.tooltip: A JavaScript regular expression, without the surrounding slashes. Capture groups appear on Groups.

ports.name: flags
ports.tooltip: Regex flags: i (ignore case), m (multiline), s (dot matches newline), u (unicode). g is controlled by Extract All.

ports.name: flushSize
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered. 0 disables size-based flushing.

ports.name: flushInterval
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically this often while items are buffered. 0 disables interval flushing.

ports.name: maxSize
ports.tooltip: Hard cap on buffered items. Overflow drops the oldest and is reported on Dropped Items. 0 means no cap.

ports.name: channel
ports.tooltip: Names the handler registry this dispatcher draws on. Leave as "default" unless two independent flows must not see each other.

ports.name: action
ports.tooltip: An action object, an array of them to run in order, or JSON text holding either.

ports.name: builtIns
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated built-in action names this dispatcher may execute: SET_STORE, MERGE_STORE, DELETE_STORE_KEY, CLEAR_STORE. Empty — the default — means a server cannot write to the store at all; everything must go through an Action Handler you wired.

ports.name: storeName
ports.tooltip: The only store the built-in actions can write. A store named inside an incoming action is ignored — the graph chooses the store, not the server.

ports.name: allowedKeys
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys the built-in store actions may write. Blank means any key of the configured store. Setting any key also refuses CLEAR_STORE.

ports.name: handlerTimeout
ports.tooltip: How long a handler has to signal Complete or Fail before the action is failed. 0 waits forever.

ports.name: waitForHandler
ports.tooltip: How long an action waits for its handler to appear before being refused as unknown — the window in which a component can still mount. 0 refuses immediately. Everything behind it waits too, because order is preserved.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.tooltip: Bound on queued actions. Overflow refuses the newest so accepted actions keep their order. 0 is unbounded.

ports.name: rateLimit
ports.tooltip: Max actions executed per window. 0 is unlimited. Excess actions are refused, not delayed.

ports.name: channel
ports.tooltip: Must match the Channel on the Action Dispatcher that should be able to reach this handler.

ports.name: actionType
ports.tooltip: The exact action type this handler accepts, e.g. OPEN_SESSION. Registering it is what makes it executable at all.

ports.name: enabled
ports.tooltip: Turning this off unregisters the handler, so the action is refused as unknown rather than quietly ignored.

ports.name: autoComplete
ports.tooltip: Report the action complete as soon as Trigger has been sent. Turn off when a later step must wait for this one to finish, and wire Complete or Fail yourself.

ports.name: result
ports.tooltip: Handed back to the dispatcher as the Result of this action when it completes.
